idiom_name: static const instance of a function-pointer table (hand-rolled vtable) with no-op operations
implementation_notes: C has no subtyping, so the classic structure is rebuilt by hand: an interface becomes a struct of function pointers, the real and the degenerate implementations are two sets of functions, and the special case is a single static const struct whose pointers target benign bodies - the shape of the kernel's /dev/null device, whose write accepts everything and whose read returns end-of-file, or of FUSE's null_oper table. What replaces the class hierarchy is therefore the table itself plus one const instance; keep construction in a factory so callers cannot mix the two. Reach for the hand-written form only when the interface is a genuine abstraction with several call sites - a single optional callback is better expressed as a NULL pointer with one guard at the call site.
pitfalls: The instance must stay static const and shared: a per-call copy defeats the point, and a mutable one invites data races when several threads use the same special case.
A NULL function pointer in the table is not a benign implementation - calling it crashes. Fill every slot with a no-op body instead of testing the pointer at each call site.
C structs carry no receiver type check, so nothing stops a caller from passing a real instance where the special case is expected; keep construction in one factory.
Returning a pointer to a heap-allocated special case transfers an ownership question to callers who were promised they could ignore the case; prefer the static instance.
